pages.text: Some types of trees can be tapped for useful fluids. Maples and Birches yield sugary saps, while Rubber Figs, Hevea and Kapok yield latex. Saps can be concentrated into syrup and used as a sweetener, while latex can be cooked with sulfur dust in a pot to make rubber bars.

Three things are required to tap a tree: the tree itself; a tree tap, which must be forged from wrought iron and placed in the middle of a trunk at least three blocks tall; and a barrel, which must be placed directly below the tap facing upward. If the conditions are right, your barrel will immediately begin to fill with sap.$(br2)In this pack, taps also work on player-grown trees - naturally generated logs are not required.

Not all trees produce all of the time. Maple and Birch trees produce sap in spring at temperatures between -4°C and 6°C, around when the snow begins to melt. Rubber Figs produce latex at 6°C or above. Hevea and Kapok need 14°C or above, and Hevea yields latex twice as fast as the others. Latitude, altitude, season and time of day all affect temperature, and thus the flow of sap.
